name: Forerunner of the Legion
oracle_text:
When this creature enters, you may search your library for a Vampire card, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top.
Whenever another Vampire you control enters, target creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
blocked_sentences: When this creature enters, you may search your library for a Vampire card, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top.

needs.what: a library search whose found card ends up on top of the library *after* the mandatory shuffle, and is revealed on the way. Concretely, `search_library` needs the shuffle to happen before the found cards are placed when the destination is the library itself -- e.g. a `destination: "library_top"` that shuffles the remaining library first and only then puts the picked card on top -- plus a `reveal: true` flag (or an implicit reveal for this destination) that emits the same public `reveal` event `op_reveal` emits, so every seat learns which card was fetched. This is the printed template of the whole Forerunner cycle and of every tutor-to-top (Vampiric Tutor, Mystical Tutor, Enlightened Tutor, Worldly Tutor, Sylvan Tutor, Ashiok's Forerunner), so the ordering and the reveal are the two things the family needs
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `search_library` is the closest op and it has `destination: "library_top"`, but `_search` in `engine/effects/ops_cards.py` calls `_move_found` first and `shuffle_library(ctx.state, pid)` second, so "library_top" plus the default shuffle puts the card on top and then immediately shuffles it back into a random position -- the exact opposite of the printed line. Reordering it by hand (a `shuffle` op, then `search_library` with `shuffle: false`) is not the DSL saying what the card says: `shuffle: false` on a library search suppresses 701.19c's mandatory shuffle, which docs/card-dsl.md states is deliberately not conditional for library searches, so the flag is being used against its documented meaning to fake an ordering the op does not offer. `look_at_top` shuffles only on request but bounds the pool to the top N cards, which turns a tutor into a gamble; `put_on_top` moves cards to the top but cannot be pointed at what a search found (see the next need)

needs.what: a way to name the cards a search just found, so a later op in the same effect list can act on exactly those cards -- `search_library` binding its picks under a name the way a trigger binds `subject`, e.g. `{"op": "search_library", ..., "as": "found"}` followed by `{"op": "reveal", "objects": {"binding": "found"}}` and `{"op": "put_on_top", "objects": {"binding": "found"}}`. This is what lets "reveal it" and "put that card on top" refer back to "a Vampire card" instead of re-choosing
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `resolve_pool` in `engine/effects/selectors.py` recognises exactly two ways to name a pool directly: `target`, which is the refs chosen for a target spec at cast time, and `binding`, which is what a *trigger* bound (`subject`, `amount`). `search_library` records nothing anywhere, so neither can reach its picks. `exiled_with` is the only other back-reference and it covers cards *this source exiled* -- `_move_found` writes no exile link, and routing the fetch through exile to borrow it would be a different set of zone changes. Re-selecting instead (`search_library` to hand, then `reveal`/`put_on_top` over `{"zone": "hand", "subtypes": ["Vampire"]}`) is a different card: it reveals every Vampire in hand rather than the one fetched, and it lets the player tuck a Vampire they were already holding
